name: uhd
desc: Hardware driver for all USRP devices
why: Driver for USRP software-defined radios, a real door into SDR hardware though it is mostly a driver layer.

brief.what_it_is: UHD (USRP Hardware Driver) is the free, open-source driver and API for Ettus Research's USRP software-defined radio hardware. It runs on the host computer and talks to USRP motherboards and daughterboards, which take in radio signals and send them to the host as samples, and which send samples back out to transmit. The README says it supports all Ettus USRP hardware, including all motherboards, daughterboards, and combinations of them. The repository holds host-side driver code, module peripheral manager (MPM) code for embedded devices, firmware, FPGA images, and tools.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames UHD as the driver and API layer for the USRP platform, so that applications can use Ettus hardware. It lists GNU Radio, MathWorks Matlab and Simulink, LabVIEW, srsRAN, OpenAirInterface, and others as the applications and toolkits built on it.
brief.how_it_works: The README describes UHD as a user-space driver with a C++ API, plus embedded MPM code that runs on the devices and firmware for the device microprocessors, and FPGA images with RFNoC (RF Network-on-Chip) as a framework for custom FPGA designs. The README does not spell out the exact data path in detail.
brief.install_notes: The README does not give install steps. It points to the UHD and USRP Manual at uhd.readthedocs.io for installation instructions and build-from-source guides. The manual's Software Installation chapter covers binary installers and source builds. The manual also covers downloading FPGA and firmware image packages, which the executables list includes as uhd_images_downloader. The README names Linux (Fedora and Ubuntu), Mac OS X, and Windows 11 as supported operating systems, and says other systems will most likely work but are not officially supported. Using real hardware means a USRP device is needed. I did not verify the Homebrew formula or its caveats.
brief.standout: UHD is the vendor-maintained, open driver that most of the SDR ecosystem sits on top of, from GNU Radio to LTE and GSM stacks. Its tooling is unusually broad: the manual is versioned (4.11.0.0 at the time of the fetch) and includes full-text search. The executables in the formula are small command-line utilities for probing devices, calibrating IQ balance and DC offset, and loading firmware and images.
brief.status: Actively maintained, as far as I could tell. The manual shows version 4.11.0.0, and the GitHub repository is the upstream Ettus Research project. I did not see a last-commit or release date on the pages I fetched, so the exact recency is unknown.
brief.caveats: The homepage is the readthedocs-style manual, not a project README, so I read the GitHub README as the main source. That README has no command lines and no install steps, so the commands list is empty. Hardware is required to do anything useful. Windows 11 and Mac OS X are supported per the README, but Linux is the primary platform. The scout note calls it a driver layer, and the README agrees: it is not a standalone SDR application.
quotes: UHD is the free & open-source software driver and API for the Universal Software Radio Peripheral (USRP™) SDR platform, created and sold by Ettus Research.
UHD supports all Ettus Research USRP™ hardware, including all motherboards and daughterboards, and the combinations thereof.
UHD is primarily developed on Linux, but we also test and support the following operating systems.
